subject.title: Bug: Orphaned TaskFlows in `waiting` status permanently block agent heartbeats (requests-in-flight deadlock)

question: What should the default abandonment semantics be for managed TaskFlows left in `waiting`, and which runtime owner should release the corresponding heartbeat busy state?
rationale: The current API intentionally supports durable waits, while the reported failure needs automatic recovery; choosing a default timeout, controller-owned deadline, manual repair path, or gateway startup sweep changes plugin/runtime contracts.

options.title: Define explicit wait abandonment
options.body: Add a controller-visible deadline, abandonment signal, or proven orphan predicate before terminalizing persisted `waiting` flows, then recover through the actual heartbeat busy-state owner.

options.title: Keep repair manual for now
options.body: Document and improve diagnostics/doctor or `tasks maintenance` repair without changing default durable wait semantics until a live deadlock proof identifies the owner.

options.title: Defer until live diagnosis
options.body: Leave the issue open for a gateway-level reproduction that distinguishes TaskFlow state, pending final delivery, active reply runs, and session lanes.

recommendation.title: Define explicit wait abandonment
recommendation.body: Add a controller-visible deadline, abandonment signal, or proven orphan predicate before terminalizing persisted `waiting` flows, then recover through the actual heartbeat busy-state owner.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent TaskFlow audit/maintenance and runtime type-surface history make this the best available owner for deciding the TaskFlow lifecycle contract.
